title: Statue of Unity Rain Forest Opens With Glass Skywalk, Artificial Rain
excerpt: The Ekta Nagar attraction, to be inaugurated by Prime Minister Modi on October 30-31, brings Western Ghats, Himalayan and Andaman flora together under a 220-metre glass skywalk — though official and earlier cost and design figures differ.
body:
• A new Rain Forest attraction at Ekta Nagar near the Statue of Unity is set to be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his October 30-31 visit to Gujarat, according to a Gujarat Chief Minister's Office release.
  • The official release puts the cost at Rs 9.49 crore for 47,000 square metres, with a 220-metre glass-deck skywalk and a 5 to 8 metre waterfall; earlier reports put the cost at about Rs 12 crore over 12 acres, with 20 rain-gun towers for artificial rain.
  • The site brings together evergreen flora from the Western Ghats, the Himalayas and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, plus an information centre and a children's activity zone.
  • For diaspora visitors planning a trip: fly to Vadodara, 90 km from Kevadia, or take a direct train to Ekta Nagar station, about 5 km from the Statue of Unity entrance.

EKTA NAGAR, Gujarat — A rainforest built in Gujarat's Narmada district, complete with a glass skywalk above the canopy, an artificial waterfall and plants collected from across India, is set to open at Ekta Nagar, the township built around the Statue of Unity.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the project during his state visit on October 30-31, according to a press release issued by the Gujarat Chief Minister's Office on Thursday and reported by Devdiscourse. The attraction aims to boost eco-tourism around the Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue.

What has been built

The official release describes a site spread across 47,000 square metres — about 11.6 acres — near the new Gora Bridge, close to the Vagadiya Checkpost, at an estimated cost of Rs 9.49 crore. Its centrepiece is a 220-metre-long glass-deck skywalk bridge, designed to give visitors a panoramic view of the forest canopy and the surrounding landscape from above.

Earlier reporting on the same project described a larger headline figure and a different skywalk design. Reports citing the initial announcement put the project at about Rs 12 crore over 12 acres, with a circular glass skywalk about 11 metres above the ground and 22 metres in diameter, made of 132 curved, toughened laminated glass panels, each 35 millimetres thick. Those reports also described 20 rain-gun towers built to simulate monsoon rainfall and hold the temperature between 25 and 30 degrees Celsius, along with bubble fountains and waterfalls. The official release issued at inauguration does not mention the rain towers, and readers should treat its Rs 9.49 crore cost and 220-metre skywalk as the latest official figures.

Flora from three regions, in one place

According to the official release, the Rain Forest is a one-stop showcase of India's diverse evergreen flora. It houses native plant and tree species collected from different ecological zones, including the Western Ghats, the Himalayas, and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Thematic landscaping is intended to depict the multi-layered canopy structure typical of tropical rainforests.

Alongside the skywalk, the site has a waterfall 5 to 8 metres high, a circular pond and connecting bridges. Its entrance gateway, 20 feet high and 40 feet wide, is built in natural stone, and trails use local Narmada stone.

For younger visitors, there is a children's activity zone with a rock-climbing wall, slides, swings and elevated tree balconies linked by stairways.

Education as well as tourism

A dedicated information centre teaches rainforest ecology, biodiversity and conservation through interactive maps, QR code-enabled displays and visual exhibits. Officials said it will also serve as a field research hub and promote local economic activity.

The new attraction joins an existing cluster at Ekta Nagar that already includes the Valley of Flowers, Jungle Safari, Cactus Garden, Butterfly Garden, Arogya Van and Vishwa Van. That cluster has been drawing growing numbers. One report on the project noted the Statue of Unity saw 58.25 lakh visitors in 2024, up 13.8 percent from 51.20 lakh in 2023, and that Ekta Nagar recorded 68.3 lakh domestic tourists in 2025, according to Trade Brains.

How diaspora visitors can reach it

Ekta Nagar, formerly Kevadia, is built for onward travel once visitors reach Gujarat. The fastest practical route is to fly into Vadodara Airport and drive the 90 kilometres to Kevadia, a journey of roughly two hours from landing to the site entrance, according to a Statue of Unity travel guide. Ahmedabad is about 200 kilometres away by road, roughly 3.5 to 4 hours.

By rail, direct trains run to Ekta Nagar, also referred to as Kevadia station, from Vadodara, Ahmedabad, Surat and Delhi, and the station is about 5 kilometres from the Statue of Unity entrance. The guide lists the statue site as open Tuesday to Sunday, closed Monday — worth checking, along with the inauguration-week schedule, before travelling.
